judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is a statutory disclosure notice reciting the TRIA definition of terrorism verbatim; the definition is long but self-contained and tracks federal law rather than creating its own boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in the Crime or General Terms sections addresses terrorism, and the notice is expressly informational; the only mild tension is with c005's statement that $-0- of premium is attributable to terrorism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain statement of the federal reimbursement formula with a fixed percentage; no term here bears two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with c003 and c004 in the same notice and is consistent with them; it creates no obligation that any operative provision contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The only defect is the OCR/typographical run-together 'ina Program Year', which does not change meaning; the $100 billion cap is a hard number.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates c004 in substance but the two are addressed to different payors (Treasury vs the Company) and can be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite dollar threshold and a pro rata mechanism keyed to Treasury procedures; nothing vague to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Restates c003 from the insurer's perspective; no operative provision of the Crime section is inconsistent with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single figure, '$ -0-'; the only question is what a zero terrorism premium signifies, which is a factual not a linguistic matter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: There is a genuine but small tension with c001, which says the policy 'makes available' terrorism insurance while no premium is charged for it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely informational text about producer compensation with a website reference; no operative language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision of the policy addresses producer compensation, so nothing to conflict with.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward statement that three named coverage sections are claims-made; the naming is specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: None of the three named sections was purchased under this policy (Item 3 lists only General Terms, Crime and Special Coverage), so the notice describes coverages that do not exist here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditional and self-limiting ('If a claims-made coverage section contains a retroactive date'); the terms are quoted and defined by reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The purchased Crime section is loss-sustained/discovery based, not claims-made, so this notice has no operative counterpart in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Describes when claims-made coverage responds; 'incidents reported' sits loosely beside 'claims actually made' but the sentence is a notice, not a grant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot be squared with the Crime section's Exclusion 19/Endorsement scheme (c110, c127, c134), which turns on loss sustained and Discovered rather than claims made.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific periods (sixty days automatic, one year optional) are stated; the caveats about 'gaps in coverage' are explanatory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It promises extended reporting periods for coverage sections not purchased here, while the Crime section provides only a sixty-day post-termination discovery window under Exclusion 19.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Marketing-style narrative about premium maturity; the only flaw is the OCR word 'matunity', which is plainly 'maturity'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No premium or rating provision elsewhere contradicts it; c033's renewal-rate mechanics are separate and compatible.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An all-caps declarations warning using defined-in-quotes terms; it is emphatic but definite about limit erosion by defense costs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It describes claims-made sections and 'DEFENSE COSTS' that this policy (Crime and Special Coverage only) does not contain, leaving a mismatch with Item 3 of the Declarations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consideration/preamble language subjecting coverage to the Declarations and other terms; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It harmonises with c047, the parallel Crime section preamble, and with c015's priority rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Coverage shall extend anywhere in the world' is a very short absolute phrase whose reach (loss location, insured location, currency) is not delimited.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pulls against Endorsement 2's sanctions exclusion (c045) and against territorially narrow Crime definitions such as Money Orders And Counterfeit Currency Fraud (c078, US/Canadian currency) and Premises (c081).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause turns on whether a General Terms provision is 'inconsistent or in conflict with' a coverage section, a judgment-laden standard that must itself be construed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is the instrument's own conflict rule and would be invoked to reconcile, for example, the General Terms notice provision (c021) with the Crime section's condition-precedent notice (c118).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is purely referential and adds no content of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Crime coverage section contains no definition of 'Claim', yet the notice provision (c021) and Endorsement/Rider 1 (c039-c043) operate on 'Claim', leaving a gap this deferral cannot fill.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line referential definition; no ambiguity on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Crime section does define Insured (c074), so the reference resolves, though Insuring Clauses 2-8 speak of 'an Organization' rather than 'an Insured'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Points to a specific Declarations item and names a single entity; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 1 names MEDIDATA SOLUTIONS INC. while Item 4 of the Crime Declarations names 'Medidate Solutions, Inc., and its subsidiaries', a spelling and scope mismatch with the Organization definition (c080).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite by reference to Item 2, with a proportionality rule for short or long periods.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 2 as printed reads 'To 42:01 A.M.', and Endorsement 3 (c130) re-keys liability to loss Discovered during the Policy Period, so the term does real and contested work.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear default rule about separate limits and retentions, expressly subject to contrary coverage-section text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Crime Subsection 25 (c116) and Item 2/Item 3 of the Crime Declarations; the built-in 'unless stated to the contrary' avoids conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mostly addresses and effective dates, but the closing sentence's 'not reasonably possible' and 'as soon as reasonably possible' are elastic standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its late-notice forgiveness must be reconciled with Crime Subsection 27's ninety-day condition precedent (c118) and with Endorsement/Rider 1's prejudice regime (c039-c041).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific currency, specific source (The Wall Street Journal) and specific trigger dates; little room to argue.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Crime Subsection 28 (c119) supplies its own valuation rules, but this clause expressly yields ('Except as otherwise provided in any coverage section').

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional subrogation language; 'everything necessary' is broad but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with the Recoveries waterfall in Crime Subsection 29 (c120), which allocates recoveries after payment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Full compliance with all the terms of this policy' as a condition precedent is a sweeping, unbounded phrase that courts often have to narrow.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits uneasily with the late-notice forgiveness in c021 and with the direct-action right created by Endorsement/Rider 1 (c043), which expressly overrides 'any other provision'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of agency functions with a parenthetical carve-out; the list is specific and closed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Insuring Clauses, which all pay 'the Parent Organization', and with Crime Subsection 21's trust arrangement for ERISA Plan losses (c112).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A strict written-endorsement requirement naming the signing authority; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The endorsements in this policy follow the stated form, though several are executed only by an 'Authorized Representative' rather than an identified Chubb & Son employee.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fixed periods (sixty days, twenty days) and a defined trigger; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Part of the closed list in Subsection 11 with (b)-(e); the 'earliest of the following times' framing keeps them coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As reproduced the paragraph carries stray subparagraph markers '(c) (d) (e) (f)' and a page break in the middle, and grounds like 'material change in the nature or extent of the risk' are open-textured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The stray markers belong to c029-c032, so the boundaries between the enumerated termination grounds and the following paragraphs are blurred on the face of the document.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fragment whose lead-in '(c)' was absorbed into the preceding text, but its content — termination by the Parent Organization on notice — is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reads coherently with c027 and c030 as part of the Subsection 11 list; no conflicting termination mechanism appears elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'At such other time as may be agreed upon' is an open term, but mutual agreement is a familiar and workable standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements rather than contradicts the other termination triggers in Subsection 11 and the prior-policy termination rule in c036.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite trigger tied to Item 2 and a cross-reference to paragraph (g); no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cross-reference to paragraph (g) resolves correctly to c033, and c033(iv) supplies a purchase right if notice is not given.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Customary short rates' is an undefined trade term whose computation is not specified anywhere in the policy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision defines or supplies a short-rate table, but nothing contradicts it either.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long and detailed with precise day counts and percentage triggers; the drafting is careful and largely self-executing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its limit-increase rule in (iii) interacts with the Policy Period definition (c019) and the Crime limits provision (c116), but the interaction is expressly provided for.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple administrative duty to copy the broker; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the notice mechanics in c021 and c035.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires stated reasons and effective date; short and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Harmonises with c028's enumerated termination reasons and c033's notice contents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Operates only on bonds or policies 'specified in Item 4', a closed reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 4 identifies policy number 8212-1392 — the same number as this policy — and the parallel Crime provision (c115) was deleted by Endorsement 3 (c129), leaving the prior-loss architecture uneven.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence preserving obligations and defenses on insolvency; standard and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses insolvency; nothing to conflict with.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A headings-are-not-terms clause, definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several operative cross-references use heading names ('Subsection 22 Legal Expenses Extension' in c098 and c118), which sits awkwardly with the statement that headings form no part of the terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Prejudiced the Company' is the operative standard and is not defined, though New York law supplies content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It changes the effect of the notice provisions in c021 and of the ninety-day condition precedent in Crime Subsection 27 (c118), which still calls timely notice a condition precedent to coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Repeats the reasonably-possible standard; elastic but familiar.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates the final paragraph of c021 almost verbatim, raising a question whether the endorsement supersedes or merely restates it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Allocates burden by a bright two-year line and creates an 'irrebuttable presumption'; the terms are precise even if severe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with c039's prejudice rule and with the two-year suit limitation in Crime Subsection 27 (c118), which runs from Discovery rather than from the notice deadline.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A negative construction rule ('nothing herein shall be construed'); its reach against the rest of the endorsement is not spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves the claims-made timing provisions, which is significant because the purchased Crime section is not claims-made at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Depends on 'death or personal injury, as that term is defined by the New York Insurance Law', an external and contested reference, and the text is interrupted by a page break.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says 'notwithstanding any other provision', which directly overrides the no-joinder and condition-precedent language in c024.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate headings and 'all other terms unchanged'; nothing to construe on its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'remain unchanged' formula becomes contestable only where two endorsements amend the same provision, which is not the case for Rider 1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Trade or economic sanctions or other similar laws or regulations' is a general catch-all appended to specific categories, and 'to the extent that' leaves the exclusion's scope undelimited.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts against the unqualified worldwide Territory clause (c014), which promises coverage 'anywhere in the world'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure boilerplate about headings and unchanged terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other endorsement touches the sanctions exclusion, so nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Consideration preamble for the Crime section; no operative content to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallels c013 and is subject to the priority rule in c015; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Turns on 'direct loss' and on the defined terms Theft and Forgery; 'direct' is the classic battleground in fidelity coverage, though here it is at least a defined-term framework.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is amended for ERISA Plan losses by Subsection 21 (c112) and narrowed by Exclusions 12(a), 12(c), 12(n) and 13 (c090, c092, c103, c104), which together substantially reshape its reach.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trailing qualifier 'committed by a Third Party' follows a four-item list (i)-(iv), leaving it unclear whether it modifies all items or only the last, a classic list-scope problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion 14 (c105) strips Forgery, Computer Fraud and other perils from this clause, and Exclusion 12(m) (c102) excludes property in a bank's custody though the clause covers Banking Premises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same trailing 'committed by a Third Party' construction after subclauses (i)-(ii), plus the odd phrase 'temporarily within the home of an Employee or an Organization'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion 12(m) (c102) excludes loss while in the custody of a person authorised to have custody, which is precisely the In Transit situation defined in c075.
